references.text: The Lord says that He will put fear and dread of Israel upon the nations, which corresponds to the promise in Exodus 23:27 to send His terror before Israel.
The Lord promises to place fear and dread of Israel over all the lands they enter, paralleling the promise to send terror ahead of the people.
Rahab reports that the inhabitants of Canaan are seized with fear of Israel, fulfilling the promise that God would send His terror before them.
The hearts of the Amorite kings melted from fear of Israel, demonstrating the fulfillment of the promise that God would send terror before His people.
Moses' song describes how fear and dread fall upon the inhabitants of Canaan, echoing the theme of God's terror going ahead of Israel.
God's dread fell upon the cities around Jacob so that they did not pursue him—an early example of God's protective terror.
Moab was seized with great fear of the people of Israel, illustrating the effect of God's terror that went before them.
God sent a trembling among the Philistines so that they fled in confusion, an example of how God made enemies turn their backs.
God's fear fell upon all the kingdoms surrounding Judah, showing God's continued fulfillment of the promise to send terror over enemies.
The psalmist confesses that victory does not come by one's own power, but through God who drives back the enemies and puts them to shame.
Deuteronomy 28:25 serves as the negative counterpart to Exodus 23:27 and shows the condition under which the promise of victory applies.
The psalm confirms the individual aspect of the promise in Exodus that God causes enemies to turn their backs.
